rules: This is legal INFORMATION, not legal advice. Every article in this cluster must say so plainly and recommend professional advice for the reader's own situation.
Cite the actual instrument by name and article number — e.g. 'Article 30 of the GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)' — and link to EUR-Lex or the Data Protection Commission.
Never paraphrase a legal obligation in a way that makes it sound weaker or narrower than the text. When in doubt, quote the condition.

The Article 30(5) derogation for organisations with fewer than 250 employees does NOT apply where the processing is likely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, where it is not occasional, or where it involves special categories of data (Article 9) or data on criminal convictions and offences (Article 10). Never present the 250-employee figure as a blanket exemption.
Ireland's supervisory authority is the Data Protection Commission (dataprotection.ie). Do not name any other Irish regulator for data protection.
If you are not confident a legal detail is accurate, leave it out and make the point qualitatively. Never guess at an article number, a deadline, or a penalty.
